title: HELLO WORLD COMPUTER
author: Han × 1001
facts: onchain — perceptron rule at question settlement
description: A perceptron that lives, learns, and answers entirely inside one contract. Input text (up to 64 bytes) is hashed into a 1024-bit feature vector of unigrams, bigrams, and trigrams; ask() sums the int32 weights at the set bits and returns a class label with a margin-based confidence. The weights started at zero — everything the model knows, someone taught it: anyone can deploy a yes/no question for a fee, the crowd answers, and each settlement runs the perceptron learning rule in contract code. Weights, training, and inference are all onchain; nothing runs anywhere else.

call.note: ask("hello world") — runs the forward pass and returns (label uint8, confidence int256)
